name: Ursula Bechtolsheimer-Kipp
current_role: Chairwoman (board president), Tschuggen Hotel Group / Tschuggen Collection (since 2016; current status not reconfirmed)
profile: German-born heiress (b. 1951), only daughter of Karl-Heinz Kipp, founder of the Massa department-store chain whose real estate was leased to Metro. She inherited much of his fortune in 2017 and chairs the family's Swiss luxury hotel group (Tschuggen Grand & Valsana Arosa, Carlton St. Moritz, Eden Roc Ascona). Lived for decades in Gloucestershire, running a horse breeding centre; now reported resident in Switzerland.
interesting_fact: The family fortune began with 500 bottles of rare wine her father sold on the post-war black market; her daughter is Olympic dressage gold medallist Laura Tomlinson.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016, alongside taking the Tschuggen chair from her 92-year-old father, she also became chair of Swiss property company Gassmann Immobilien- und Beteiligungs-AG and backed the Massa Nova project in Chur with her son Götz (per Bilanz).

public_contacts.value: c.maerzheuser@tschuggencollection.ch (Constanze Märzheuser, Director of PR, Tschuggen Collection)

notes: Very private; no personal social accounts found. Best route is the Tschuggen Collection PR director. Husband Wilfried died 2020 (avoid). Was dropped from Forbes real-time list after 2021.

name: Dmitry Pumpansky
current_role: Former owner and chairman of TMK (Russian steel-pipe maker); left TMK's board and beneficial ownership in March 2022
profile: Russian industrialist (b. 1964, usually spelled Dmitry Pumpyansky), graduate of the Ural Polytechnic Institute. Started as a metals trader, ran pipe plants including Sinarsky, joined TMK in 2002 and by 2006 owned 100% of it, building one of the world's largest makers of oil-and-gas tubulars. Said to have exited TMK in 2022; reported living in Geneva.
interesting_fact: After co-buying TMK with Sergei Popov and Andrey Melnichenko, he bought both partners out in 2006 to become its sole owner.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 he earned a Doctor of Technical Sciences degree with a dissertation on steels, alloys and production technologies for next-generation OCTG and specialty pipes, adding to his earlier engineering candidate degree and economics doctorate.
notes: Name in input is a variant spelling of Pumpyansky. Sanctioned by UK (2022) and named on the US CAATSA list; EU sanctions annulled by the EU General Court on appeal. Outreach carries compliance/reputational risk; no published personal or office contact found.

name: Maurizio Billi
current_role: Controlling shareholder and chairman/president of Eurofarma (Brazilian pharma group)
profile: Son of Italian chemist Galliano Billi, who founded Eurofarma in 1972. Maurizio joined as a teenager, took over as president in 2000 and turned it into one of Brazil's largest drugmakers, expanding via acquisitions across Latin America (operations in 20+ countries, 12,600+ staff). Still leads the company and its strategy.
interesting_fact: An avid racer: his Eurofarma team has repeatedly won Stock Car Brasil titles, and in 2013 he himself won a race in the Porsche Master Cup Brasil.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in 1957, the same year his parents emigrated from Italy to South America, and at 19 (1976) started helping his father's small company, rotating through production, finance, purchasing and HR before becoming president in 2000.
notes: Described by Forbes Brasil as discreet. No published press email found; Eurofarma site blocks scraping. Sources differ on title (president vs chairman of the board); company 2024 report signs him as Presidente do Conselho.
